title: OptiRange: An Efficient ReRAM-Based PIM Accelerator with ADC Resolution Optimization
problem: ReRAM-based in-memory computing (IMC) accelerators suffer from high energy consumption in ADCs and throughput limitations when using low-resolution ADCs or shared ADC architectures. Maintaining model accuracy while reducing ADC cost is a key bottleneck.
motivation: Mitigating the memory wall for DNN inference through energy-efficient in-memory computing while reducing the area and power overhead of peripheral ADC circuits is critical for practical PIM deployment.
method: OptiRange reduces energy waste in ReRAM-based processing-in-memory accelerators by making ADCs (analog-to-digital converters) do less work. The Split-the-Burden algorithm shifts stored values toward zero so ADCs need less precision to convert them. A second technique adapts each column's ADC range at runtime and skips unnecessary conversions. The third technique uses varying computation times across columns to keep the system busy and boost throughput while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: By independently rearranging ReRAM values and adapting each column's ADC range, OptiRange cuts energy waste without changing the underlying computation.
contributions: Split-the-Burden algorithm for cell value manipulation that reduces LRS cells and lowers fixed ADC resolution requirements
Dynamic ADC range adaptation at software level enabling selective skipping of conversion cycles
ADC range-based grouping strategy for improved synchronization and system throughput
Experimental validation showing significant energy and performance improvements over conventional ReRAM accelerators

metrics.other: reduced ADC resolution and LRS cell count

limitations: Specific performance numbers and comparisons on standard benchmarks are not detailed in the abstract, and scalability to larger networks is not explicitly discussed.
